'''Michael Gross''' (3 November 1963, [[Kirn]], Germany) is a British science writer based at [[Oxford]] and has been awarded an honorary research fellowship at the School of Crystallography, [[Birkbeck, University of London]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Michael Gross |url=https://press.jhu.edu/books/authors/michael-gross |access-date=20 May 2023 |publisher=Hopkins Press |publication-place=Baltimore, Maryland}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=10 July 2013 |title=MIchael Gross |url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/H1000302682/BIC?u=wikipedia&sid=bookmark-BIC&xid=5adcc592 |access-date=20 May 2023 |website=Gale Literature: Contemporary Authors |publisher=[[Gale (publisher)|Gale]]}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Gross studied engineering and chemistry at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]], and he holds a doctorate in physical biochemistry from [[University of Regensburg|Regensburg University]], both German institutions.<ref name=":1" /> During seven years of post-doctoral research in protein biochemistry at the [[University of Oxford]], he wrote science journalism as a hobby. In 2000, he switched to writing full-time. Occasionally he also acts as a translator, editor, and lecturer.  As of 2013, Gross was married and had three children.<ref name=":1" />

== Works ==
Gross has been working as a science journalist since 1993, and became a "science writer in residence" at [[Birkbeck College]] in 2001.<ref name=":1" />  Gross is the author of around 30 research papers, over 700 journalistic pieces, and seven books, including ''Life on the Edge,''<ref name=":0" /> ''Travels to the Nanoworld,'' and ''Light and Life.'' He writes in English and German and parts of his work have been translated into French, Spanish and Italian. He is married with three children and lives in Oxford.
